text:
julia: FYI saw a regression after yesterday's mixed-quant deploy to canary. Eval suite shows +3.8% hallucination rate and a couple JSON schema breaks on structured responses for model: redwood-7b-mixfp8-int4.

sam: ugh. was that the kernel-selection tweak we pushed? saw a latency dip but maybe quality tradeoff. can you paste the failing eval ids?

julia: failing evals: eval_2026_prod_prompt_118, eval_2026_prod_prompt_271. Both produce truncated JSON fields (missing "items" key) and extra hallucinated sentences. Also end-to-end p99 latency up ~12% on small-seq traffic.

mike: attaching quick profile snapshot from canary (top kernels):
```
Kernel                    time_ms   calls
fp8_attention_forward     1340      14200
int4_attention_forward    780       9200
kv_cache_read             210       48000
kv_cache_miss             48        1200
batcher_dispatch          420       5600
```
Notes: fp8_attention_forward time jumped vs baseline by ~18% for short seqs (<64).

anya: I think this is the selector bug I mentioned in PR #4212 — the threshold for falling back to int4 was loosened, so short-context requests are being routed to fp8 kernels which expect different KV packing. That misalignment creates off-by-one token offsets in cached streams -> structured output breaks.

julia: can you point to the config that changed? rough timeline?

anya: change landed yesterday @ 03:12 UTC. config: `selector.min_seq_for_fp8 = 32` (was 64). rationale was to improve throughput for short requests, but we didn't validate kv alignment on prefix caching.

sam: that explains the p99 bump — fp8 kernels have higher per-call overhead for small sequences due to extra quant/dequant steps. Also kv_cache_read shows a nontrivial miss rate; maybe packing differences cause stale lookups.

mike: I repro'd locally with a small harness. Repro steps:
1) checkout canary branch
2) run `./bin/serving-bench --model redwood-7b-mixfp8-int4 --seq 8 --batch 1 --kv-prefix=enabled --runs 500`
3) observe JSON-misalignment on outputs and compare `kv_cache_miss` counters

Example log excerpt showing misaligned tokens:
```
[2026-03-17T10:02:12Z] request_id=abc123 token_idx=23 emitted_token="," expected=":"
[2026-03-17T10:02:12Z] request_id=abc123 kv_read_index=45 computed_index=44
```

ci-bot: perf-regression alert triggered: eval-suite/hallucination +3.8% vs baseline at 2001000000. Canary flagged.

julia: ok, immediate mitigation: revert selector change in canary and bump config back to 64. Can we roll that in now and monitor evals?

anya: I can push a hotfix to revert the config and add a guard that prevents fp8 routing unless `kv_compat=true`. Will open PR and request urgent review.

mike: in parallel we should add a unit test in runtime that verifies KV index stability across kernel paths. I sketched one: feed same prefix to fp8 and int4 paths and assert identical post-kv offsets.

sam: agree. also let's add telemetry: tag requests routed to fp8 when seq<64 and emit `kv_alignment_warning` metric so we can catch regressions earlier.

ops-bot: @{julia,anya} deploying config revert to canary pool now (rolling restart). Tracking: deploy-7894. ETA ~4m.

julia: thanks. after revert, we'll run the eval subset: eval_118 and eval_271 only, and an internal smoke on JSON schema checks.

mike: post-revert, I expect hallucination delta to fall back to baseline. If not, we'll need to look at calibration artifacts — calibration table changes (scale/zero) can still cause token distribution shifts. I saved the calibration maps: `calib_fp8_v2026_03_16` vs `calib_fp8_v2026_03_17`.

anya: good call. I'll diff the two calibration artifacts as a follow-up. For now, PR #4220 reverts selector and adds `kv_compat` safety gate.

julia: owners: anya -> hotfix + PR, mike -> unit test + repro harness, sam -> telemetry metric and dashboard. I'll run the two evals after deploy and post results in thread.

sam: added dashboard panel: /dash/eng-runtime/kv_alignment_fp8_vs_int4

julia: quick post-deploy update: deploy finished, canary restarted. Running eval subset now.

julia: eval_118: passed schema checks. eval_271: schema pass, hallucination delta reduced to +0.4% (within noise). p99 latency back to baseline.

mike: confirmed local harness returns aligned kv indices after revert. Leaving a TODO to harden kernel selector tests.

anya: opened follow-ups: #4221 (calib diff analysis), #4222 (unit test), #4223 (telemetry alert rule). Leaving notes in PR.

julia: good work. We'll keep canary under watch for 24h. If anything else shows up, re-open. :thumbsup:
